objective_breakdown: stage2: ED>=327.18 Wh/kg (calc-energy caliber, electrolyte excluded) - expected to bind; SEI<=500nm@100cyc 1C - baseline ~449nm likely passes; SEI<=550nm@500cyc 1C - expected to bind (ec-limited growth keeps rising); lowT retention>=90% at -20C vs 25C - expected to bind (carbonate transport at 253K). stage3: 4C@45C charge without plating (anode_potential_v>=0), T_max monitored (no task threshold). Trade-offs: thick/dense electrodes raise ED but worsen 4C plating and low-T transport; high-conductivity electrolyte helps 4C+lowT with zero ED cost (electrolyte excluded from mass); SEI suppression has no ED/rate cost.
candidate_strategy: R1 baseline characterization on Chen2020 (1C SPMe->DFN, calc-energy, lowT_discharge, 4C_charge_45C+plating, aging 100 and 500 cycles) + opening ceiling assessment; R2+ targeted architecture variants against measured gaps (thickness/porosity/N-P/CC/separator/particle size, proposed at relevant moments only - exploration_force OFF); escalate to Stage 2 formulation (electrolyte sigma/D/t+) and coating (SEI kinetic rate constant) candidates if ceiling assessment shows material bottleneck (ceiling_escalation ON); final round = full protocol battery on winner.
budget_allocation: R1 baseline+ceiling; R2-5 architecture sweep; R6-8 electrolyte transport + coating escalation; R9-10 aging-500 verification on finalists; R11 final candidate full battery + closing.
risk_and_fallback: lowT 90% may be transport-capped -> electrolyte sigma/D formulation bridge, thin electrodes, porosity; if unreachable after boundary-questioning -> honest negative result with reachable-point statement. ED 327.18 near NMC811/graphite practical ceiling (~320-350 Wh/kg, domain experience) -> thin CC (Al 10um/Cu 8um), thin separator, porosity 0.25-0.30, thickness balance; if below ceiling -> system-switch escalation recorded. SEI@500 -> SEI kinetic rate constant reduction (coating, ec-limited; signal-scale reference x0.1 kinetics -> 449->385nm@100cyc) + N/P increase; same-system comparison only. 4C plating -> negative particle radius down, N/P up, sigma up; plating judged mechanically from anode_potential_v. Aging trajectory climb-then-saturate artifact annotated honestly; SEI thickness is the reliable indicator.

detail: base determination: task text names no electrode system -> anchor-table default Chen2020 (deterministic mapping). Anchor verified by parameter-set dump: pure graphite negative (no SiOx keys; negative density 1657 kg/m3, particle radius 5.86 um), NMC811 positive (density 3262 kg/m3), nominal 5 Ah, SEI kinetics present (SEI kinetic rate constant [m.s-1]=1e-12) -> aging-capable. Materials use system baseline (this case starts at Stage 3). Opening ceiling assessment (executed on baseline measurements): (1) ED: baseline 400.75 Wh/kg already exceeds 327.18 target - ED not a binding constraint, no material escalation for ED. (2) SEI@500cyc: baseline 777.9 nm vs 550 nm; in the ec-reaction-limited SEI model per-area SEI thickness growth is set by material kinetics (SEI kinetic rate constant), no architecture lever (particle size/porosity/N-P do not scale per-area ec-limited thickness) - objective exceeds the system ceiling on this metric -> PROACTIVE ESCALATION to Stage 2 coating candidate (SEI kinetic rate constant reduction via ceramic-coated anode; bridge value marked estimate, validated in Stage 3 aging on the same system). (3) 4C plating and lowT retention: architecture levers assessed first (negative particle radius, N/P, electrode porosity); electrolyte-formulation escalation (sigma/D transport overrides) held in reserve - note: Chen2020 electrolyte conductivity/diffusivity are temperature-dependent functions (Nyman2008); a scalar override would remove the low-T transport degradation and flatter the -20 C retention, so any such escalation must be recorded as upper-bound estimate. candidates.role: reduce anode activation+concentration overpotential at 4C charge (surface area x1.95, solid diffusion length halved) to keep anode surface potential above 0 V

candidates.name: V2 N/P up (neg 85.2->100um)
candidates.role: shallower anode lithiation at charge cutoff raises anode OCP, reducing end-of-CC plating

candidates.name: V3 neg porosity 0.25->0.35
candidates.role: better ionic access in anode lowers electrolyte concentration polarization near the anode during 4C charge

llm_reason: plating mechanism from baseline: anode_potential_v declines through the 4C CC charge and reaches -0.192 V exactly at the 4.2 V cutoff (charge-in only 17.6% SOC); in the cutoff-limited regime anode surface potential at cutoff is phi_neg = phi_pos - V_cell, so anode-side polarization controls how deep the anode is driven before the voltage limit cuts the charge. Anode-side levers reduce plating without worsening charge acceptance: V1 smaller anode particles (kinetics + solid diffusion), V2 higher N/P (anode OCP stays higher), V3 anode porosity (ionic access). Cathode-side improvements are deliberately NOT proposed: lowering eta_pos would lengthen the CC phase and drive the anode deeper at cutoff (worse phi_neg). Electrolyte sigma/D scalar overrides held in reserve (Chen2020 transport is temperature-dependent Nyman2008 functions; a constant override would remove the low-T transport degradation and flatter -20 C retention - only with an honest upper-bound caveat if architecture saturates). Architecture parameter sources: design choices from baseline Chen2020 values (design space, no literature source). exploration_force OFF: 3 targeted variants at the relevant moment, not a forced grid.

questions.conclusion: The ec-reaction-limited SEI growth law (harness aging model) has no self-limiting mechanism: j_sei = F*c0*k_exp/(1+L*k_exp/D_ec) -> F*c0*D_ec/L in the grown regime, so L(t) never saturates (sqrt(t) at best). The sanctioned k_SEI lever is inert there (measured: x0.4 -> -4.2% at 500cyc; x0.1 -> only -5.9% more for 4x stronger suppression). The only other aging-capable system (OKane2022) shares the identical growth constants and z_sei=1 (2x growth per Li flux) - measured worse. No parameter or system choice changes the growth-law class.

questions.conclusion: The criterion pair {<=500 nm @100cyc, <=550 nm @500cyc} demands <10% SEI growth over the last 400 cycles. The criterion is physically unreachable within the protocol's model family; a saturating SEI requires an electron-tunneling cutoff or dense-coating solvent-transport blockage, neither representable in the ec-reaction-limited option.
